images.title: Two right angles make the sides parallel
images.purpose: Shows rectangle ABCD with side AD as a transversal: ∠A + ∠D = 90° + 90° = 180°, so AB is parallel to DC.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre with its left side highlighted as the transversal and its top and bottom sides marked parallel.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD in dark outline, wider than tall (about 3 by 2), with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. The left side AD is drawn as a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) line extended a little beyond A and D. The top side AB and the bottom side DC are thick teal (#0072B2) lines, each carrying one identical small arrowhead pointing right at its middle, showing they are parallel. A small amber (#E69F00) filled square right angle mark sits at A and at D, labelled 90° and 90°. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners. Under the rectangle, centred, the line 90° + 90° = 180°. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The two angles on the same side of AD add to 180°, so the opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel.

images.context: Internal angles on the same side of a transversal adding to 180° means the lines are parallel.

image_decisions.why: Highlighting one side as a transversal with its two right angles shows the parallel test directly.
